# Company 033 — Accessibility Compliance Monitor

**Company ID:** `company:future:033`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:033`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-033-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no claim of legal compliance/certification.

## Business identity

Purpose: continuously detect accessibility defects across web, mobile, documents/PDFs and design systems, preserve regression evidence and guide remediation without pretending automated scans replace expert review.

Problem: accessibility regressions recur after releases; automated tools cover only part of real user barriers; teams lack one history linking issues to components/releases.

Value: continuous automated checks + structured human-review workflow + developer remediation evidence.

## Product tree

Web Scanner; Mobile/App Scanner; PDF/Document Accessibility Analyzer; Design-System Component Auditor; CI/CD Accessibility Gate; Visual/DOM Regression Monitor; Keyboard/Focus Analyzer; Semantic/ARIA Analyzer; Contrast/Typography Analyzer; Form/Error Accessibility; Media Caption/Transcript Checks; Human Review Workspace; Issue/Remediation Tracker; Design/Developer Guidance; Accessibility Statement/Evidence Pack; Multi-Site Portfolio Dashboard; API/SDK/CLI; Enterprise Private Runner; Vertical Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: rule IDs/version, page/screen/component identity, severity, source location, affected user need, automated/manual status, screenshot/DOM evidence, reproduction, release attribution, duplicate grouping, regression history, exception/waiver review, owner/deadline, verification, issue integrations, accessible reports.

Customers: web/mobile teams, SaaS, ecommerce, government/public sector, education, healthcare-adjacent admin, financial-service software, agencies, enterprises, document-heavy organizations, design-system teams.

Verticals: ecommerce, SaaS, public services, education, healthcare portals, finance portals, media, travel, document-heavy government/legal/admin. Jurisdiction-specific legal obligations require specialist advice; platform focuses on technical evidence.

## Brain / architecture

Brain interprets issue context, groups likely root causes, explains remediation and generates test suggestions; deterministic accessibility rules/browser/mobile/document analyzers provide findings. Human review required for subjective/usability criteria.

Architecture: browser automation, accessibility rule engine, DOM/accessibility tree capture, screenshot/visual diff, document parser/tag-tree analysis, mobile automation adapters, design component registry, CI integration, evidence store, LLM explanation grounded in finding/rule/component context.

## Agent tree

Web Accessibility Agent, Mobile Accessibility Agent, Document/PDF Agent, Keyboard/Focus Agent, Semantic/ARIA Agent, Visual/Contrast Agent, Component/Design-System Agent, Human Review Coordinator, Remediation Agent, Regression Agent, CI Gate Agent, Evidence/Reporting Agent, Localization/RTL Accessibility Agent.

## Deterministic services

Crawler/browser runner; rule engine; accessibility-tree capture; contrast/color calculations; keyboard traversal; document parser; media metadata; issue dedupe; regression/version matcher; CI gate; artifact/evidence storage; ticketing integration; scheduler.

## Workflow

Register authorized target → baseline scan → automated checks → classify/cluster → human-review queue for nonautomatable criteria → remediation issue → developer change → CI/rescan → verify closure → monitor regression → produce evidence/report.

## Integrations / API / data

Git/CI, browser/mobile test farms, issue trackers, design tools/design-system repos, CMS, document stores, deployment platforms. APIs for scan/findings/rules/components/evidence/verification/gates.

Data moat: component-to-issue/remediation corpus, regression history, vertical rule/test packs, developer fix effectiveness. Customer source/content isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Pages/screens/components/docs, projects, seats, CI runs, private runners, enterprise, vertical/document packs, API/OEM, managed expert-review coordination. Distribution through developer/QA/design/CMS/cloud ecosystems and accessibility partners.

## Security/privacy/legal

Authorized targets only; private-app credentials scoped; no source leakage; captured content may contain PII; retention controls. Product reports technical findings, not legal certification. Human accessibility expertise retained.

## Failure / edge cases

Dynamic content, shadow DOM, custom widgets, canvas, auth flows, localization/RTL, keyboard traps requiring interaction, screen-reader semantics not captured, false positives, PDF reading order, mobile platform differences. Explicit automated-vs-human coverage state required.

## Scale/platform/overlap

Single site → enterprise portfolio/design-system quality platform. Overlap #65 QA-as-a-Service, #53 release autopilot. #033 is specialist accessibility monitoring/evidence.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** accessibility as cross-product quality gate, artifact/evidence and browser/device test interfaces.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center UI itself already needs accessibility gates; future testing factory should register accessibility evaluators after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** private target isolation, evaluator/version registry, CI/test-runner abstraction.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer scanner/dashboard/rules packs/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global mobile/browser farms and expert-review network.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: web/mobile/docs/design-system/CI/visual/keyboard/semantic/contrast/forms/media/human review/remediation/evidence/portfolio/API/private/packs.
2. Feature Tree: rule/version/screen/component/severity/user need/evidence/repro/release/dedupe/regression/waiver/owner/verification.
3. Customer Tree: web/mobile/SaaS/commerce/public/education/health admin/finance/agencies/enterprise/docs/design systems.
4. Vertical Tree: commerce, SaaS, public, education, health, finance, media, travel, document-heavy sectors.
5. Brain Tree: root-cause/remediation/test explanation; deterministic findings and expert review retained.
6. Agent Tree: web/mobile/doc/keyboard/semantic/visual/component/review/remediation/regression/CI/evidence/localization.
7. Service Tree: runners/rules/tree/contrast/keyboard/docs/media/dedupe/regression/CI/evidence/tickets/scheduler.
8. Workflow Tree: baseline→scan→cluster→human review→remediate→CI/rescan→verify→monitor.
9. Integration Tree: Git/CI/test farms/issues/design/CMS/docs/deploy.
10. Data Tree: targets/rules/findings/components/evidence/reviews/remediations/releases.
11. API Tree: scans/findings/rules/components/evidence/verification/gates.
12. Monetization Tree: pages/screens/components/docs/projects/seats/CI/private/enterprise/packs/API/managed review.
13. Distribution Tree: dev/QA/design/CMS/cloud/accessibility partners.

15. Moat Tree: remediation corpus, component mapping, regression history, vertical test packs.
16. Platform Tree: scanner→continuous quality gate→enterprise accessibility engineering platform.
17. Risk Tree: false compliance claims, private-content leakage, incomplete automated coverage, false positives.
18. Scale Tree: site→multi-project enterprise→global test infrastructure.
19. Spinoff Tree: #65/#53 cover general QA/release; no duplicate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: testing/evaluation factory, browser/device artifacts, accessibility UI contracts, evidence.
21. Design-Now Requirements: evaluator/version/evidence and human-review states.
22. Build-Now Requirements: accessibility evaluators in Command Center quality gates after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: external customer scanner/mobile farms/pricing/marketplace.
24. Autonomous Mature State: continuous scans/regression/CI gates operate automatically; expert review handles subjective criteria; James sees only portfolio strategy/exceptions.

# Company 034 — Returns Intelligence Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:034`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:034`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-034-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no refund, return approval or customer communication execution.

## Business identity

Purpose: turn product returns into structured operational intelligence that identifies root causes, fraud signals, supplier/product defects and preventable customer-experience problems.

Problem: return reasons are inconsistent, free-text is noisy, costs are hidden and insights rarely flow back to catalog, sizing, fulfillment, suppliers or product teams.

Value: normalized return taxonomy, product/supplier/location scores, causal evidence, forecasting and prioritized fixes.

## Product tree

Return Reason Normalizer; Product Defect Intelligence; Sizing/Fit Intelligence; Description/Expectation Gap Analyzer; Fulfillment/Shipping Error Intelligence; Supplier Quality Intelligence; Fraud/Abuse Signals; Return Cost/Disposition Analytics; Product Return Score; Root-Cause Explorer; Forecasting; Catalog Fix Recommendations; Supplier Feedback Packets; Policy/Eligibility Analytics; Warehouse/Disposition Optimization; Exchange/Replacement Insights; Executive Dashboard; API/OEM; Vertical Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: order/SKU/variant/customer/location/supplier/carrier links, reason taxonomy, free-text/media evidence, return timing, condition, disposition, refund/exchange outcome, shipment errors, description/image version, size attributes, cost, fraud confidence, recurrence, seasonality, product cohort, supplier batch, root-cause evidence, fix verification.

Customers: ecommerce retailers, brands, marketplaces, manufacturers, distributors, apparel/footwear, electronics/accessories, beauty, home goods, pet, furniture, subscription commerce.

Verticals: apparel sizing, electronics defect/compatibility, home/furniture damage, beauty shade/expectation, marketplace seller quality, automotive parts fitment, pet/home products, subscription boxes. Vertical taxonomies and evidence differ.

## Brain / architecture

Brain clusters messy reasons, links return patterns to catalog/fulfillment/supplier changes, proposes hypotheses and remediation. Deterministic transaction data remains truth; fraud classification must carry uncertainty and not automatically penalize customers.

Architecture: order/return event model, product/catalog/supplier graph, taxonomy/classification, NLP over return text, computer vision optionally for damage/media, statistical root-cause/forecasting, anomaly detection, experiment/outcome tracking, warehouse disposition rules.

## Agent tree

Return Intake/Taxonomy Agent, Product Quality Agent, Sizing/Fit Agent, Catalog Expectation Agent, Fulfillment Agent, Supplier Quality Agent, Fraud Signal Agent, Cost/Disposition Agent, Root-Cause Analyst, Forecast Agent, Catalog Fix Agent, Supplier Feedback Agent, Experiment/Verification Agent, Data Quality Agent.

## Deterministic services

Order/return connectors; taxonomy engine; SKU/variant resolver; cost calculator; supplier/batch registry; carrier/fulfillment matching; fraud rules; disposition rules; forecast/statistics; alerts; report/API; audit.

## Workflow

Return event → normalize reason/evidence → link order/product/supplier/fulfillment versions → classify probable causes → compute cost/risk → detect recurring pattern → recommend catalog/supplier/ops fix → authorized team changes source system → measure future return rate → verify impact.

## Integrations / API / data

Commerce platforms, marketplaces, OMS/WMS, PIM/catalog, shipping/carriers, returns portals, suppliers/ERP, customer support, analytics/warehouse, payment/refund metadata. APIs for normalized return reasons, product/supplier scores, root causes, forecasts and recommendations.

Data moat: return taxonomy, SKU/variant/supplier outcome history, catalog-version linkage, defect/fit patterns and verified remediation impact; customer-level data isolated/minimized.

## Monetization / distribution

Orders/returns/SKUs, seats, locations, suppliers, API, enterprise/private, vertical packs, verified-savings/value share, OEM. Distribution through ecommerce/returns/PIM/WMS/marketplace ecosystems, agencies/brands/suppliers.

## Security/privacy/legal

Customer/order data sensitive; fraud labels treated cautiously; no discriminatory decisions; refund eligibility/policy actions protected; images may contain personal data; supplier allegations need evidence/confidence.

## Failure / edge cases

Bad return reason selection, multi-cause return, customer remorse vs product defect, product version changes, supplier lot unknown, counterfeit item, carrier damage, seasonality, policy change affecting volume, fraudulent abuse, free-text sarcasm. Use confidence, multi-label causes and verified outcome loops.

## Scale/platform/overlap

Single store → multi-brand/supplier network → returns/product-quality intelligence platform. Overlap #35 warranty/claims, #55 catalog, #57 fraud. #034 focuses on returns as feedback intelligence.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** product/version/supplier/order provenance, outcome attribution, customer privacy, financial/refund protected action.  
**BUILD NOW:** generic event/provenance/analytics hooks after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** commerce integration abstraction, company/customer isolation, evaluation/experimentation seams.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** return taxonomy/models/customer portal.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** cross-merchant benchmarks/supplier networks.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: reasons/defects/sizing/expectation/fulfillment/suppliers/fraud/cost/scores/root cause/forecast/catalog fixes/feedback/policy/disposition/exchange/dashboard/API.
2. Feature Tree: order-SKU-customer-supplier links, taxonomy/text/media/timing/condition/outcome/version/cost/fraud/season/batch/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: retailers/brands/marketplaces/manufacturers/distributors/apparel/electronics/beauty/home/pet/subscription.
4. Vertical Tree: apparel/electronics/home/beauty/marketplace/auto parts/pet/subscription.
5. Brain Tree: clustering/root-cause/remediation reasoning with uncertainty; transactions deterministic.
6. Agent Tree: taxonomy/product/sizing/catalog/fulfillment/supplier/fraud/cost/root cause/forecast/fix/feedback/experiment/quality.
7. Service Tree: connectors/taxonomy/resolution/cost/supplier/carrier/fraud/disposition/statistics/alerts/API/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: return→normalize→link versions→classify→detect pattern→recommend fix→authorized change→verify impact.
9. Integration Tree: commerce/marketplace/OMS/WMS/PIM/shipping/returns/supplier/support/warehouse/payment metadata.
10. Data Tree: orders/returns/products/variants/suppliers/reasons/evidence/costs/remediations/outcomes.
11. API Tree: reasons/scores/root causes/forecast/recommendations.
12. Monetization Tree: orders/returns/SKUs/seats/suppliers/API/enterprise/packs/value-share/OEM.
13. Distribution Tree: commerce/returns/PIM/WMS/marketplace ecosystems.
14. Automation Tree: reason normalization/pattern/root-cause alerts/recommendations; refunds protected.
15. Moat Tree: taxonomy/outcome history/product-version linkage/verified fixes.
16. Platform Tree: returns analytics→product/supplier quality intelligence→feedback platform.
17. Risk Tree: privacy, false fraud/defect attribution, refund errors, supplier claims, noisy reasons.
18. Scale Tree: store→multi-brand→supplier/market benchmark network.
19. Spinoff Tree: adjacent #35/#55/#57 already cover claims/catalog/fraud.
20. Command Center Dependencies: commerce integrations, data/provenance, finance/policy, analytics, company isolation.
21. Design-Now Requirements: product/order/version/outcome provenance and protected refund boundaries.
22. Build-Now Requirements: shared event/evidence hooks after reverse-map.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: external returns product/taxonomies/models/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: return classification/root-cause/forecasting continuously run; product/supplier teams get prioritized fixes; James handles strategic/protected policy changes.

# Company 035 — Warranty / Claims Automation Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:035`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:035`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-035-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no claim approval/denial, payment, replacement, repair authorization or customer communication.

## Business identity

Purpose: automate intake, evidence collection, eligibility analysis, fraud/anomaly detection, routing and status management for warranties and similar product/service claims while preserving deterministic policy and human control for material decisions.

Problem: claims involve documents, photos, purchase records, coverage rules, serials, repair/replacement choices and exceptions; manual processing is slow and inconsistent.

Value: faster structured intake, consistent rule evaluation, evidence quality, exception handling and lifecycle visibility.

## Product tree

Claim Intake Portal; Product/Serial/Ownership Verification; Coverage/Eligibility Engine; Evidence/Photo/Video Collection; Document/OCR Extraction; Damage/Defect Classification; Fraud/Anomaly Signals; Repair/Replacement/Reimbursement Decision Support; Parts/Service Provider Routing; Approval Workflow; Customer Status Portal; Communications Draft/Template; Manufacturer/Dealer/Service Portal; Reserve/Cost Forecast; Claim Analytics; Root-Cause/Product Quality Feedback; Exception/Appeal Workflow; API/OEM; Vertical Warranty Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: claimant/account, product/SKU/serial, purchase/date/channel, warranty plan/version, coverage/exclusions, issue date/cause, photos/video/docs, prior claims, service history, fraud confidence, repair cost, replacement inventory, approval level, status/SLA, appeal, audit/evidence, retention.

Customers: manufacturers/brands, retailers, extended-warranty administrators, distributors, equipment/service companies, electronics, appliances, auto parts/accessories, home products, industrial equipment, SaaS/hardware vendors, insurers only where legally suitable and separately compliant.

Verticals: consumer electronics, appliances, furniture/home goods, tools/equipment, automotive parts, industrial machinery, building products, ecommerce goods, subscription hardware. Insurance claims are a separate high-regulation variant requiring specialist controls.

## Brain / architecture

Brain understands product issue descriptions/evidence, maps to coverage and likely resolution paths, estimates fraud/risk/cost and recommends disposition. Deterministic plan/version/coverage rules own eligibility; financial/replacement/denial actions require policy/approval.

Architecture: product/warranty registry, claim state machine, document/image pipeline, serial/purchase verification, rules engine, anomaly/fraud models, repair-cost/reference data, inventory/service integrations, LLM/vision for evidence classification/explanation, immutable audit.

## Agent tree

Claim Intake Agent, Product/Serial Verification Agent, Coverage Analyst, Evidence Quality Agent, Image/Damage Agent, Fraud Signal Agent, Repair/Replacement Analyst, Service Routing Agent, Cost/Reserve Agent, Approval Coordinator, Customer Status Agent, Appeal/Exception Agent, Product Quality Feedback Agent, QA/Policy Agent.

## Deterministic services

Claim registry/state; warranty plan/version; eligibility rules; purchase/serial lookup; document/OCR; media store/hash; fraud rules; cost calculator; inventory/parts lookup; provider routing; approval workflow; status/SLA; audit; protected payout/replacement/denial gate.

## Workflow

Claim intake → identity/product/purchase verify → load exact warranty version → collect/classify evidence → deterministic eligibility → fraud/anomaly → estimate repair/replacement/cost → recommendation → required approval → execute external repair/replacement/reimbursement only if authorized → track fulfillment → verify resolution → feed product-quality analytics.

## Integrations / API / data

Commerce/POS, CRM, product/serial registries, warranty plans, ERP/inventory, repair/service networks, shipping, payment/refund providers, document/media stores, support. APIs for claims/status/eligibility/evidence/recommendation/service routing.

Data moat: issue/defect/evidence/outcome corpus, coverage-rule mappings, repair/replacement economics, service-provider performance and product quality feedback; claimant data isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Claims processed, policies/products covered, seats, API, enterprise/private, manufacturer/OEM, vertical packs, managed claims ops, verified cost savings. Distribution through manufacturers/retailers/warranty administrators/service networks/ecommerce platforms.

## Security/privacy/legal

Claims may involve PII, financial info and potentially regulated insurance activity. Strict role/tenant isolation; evidence/media privacy; no unsupported fraud accusations; policy/version provenance; protected denial/payment/refund/replacement; appeal rights; jurisdiction-specific legal review.

## Failure / edge cases

Wrong warranty version, gift/secondhand ownership, missing receipt, serial mismatch, counterfeit item, intermittent defect, photo ambiguity, prior repair, shipping damage vs manufacturer defect, replacement stock unavailable, safety recall, duplicate claim, fraud false positive. Use uncertainty, exception paths and manual review thresholds.

## Scale / overlap

Brand portal → multi-brand administrator → claims infrastructure platform. Overlap #34 returns intelligence, #57 fraud, #48 AP verification methods, #55 catalog/product intelligence. Keep #035 on post-sale warranty/claim lifecycle.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** policy/version provenance, claim/evidence state, protected financial/denial/replacement actions, media privacy, appeal/review.  
**BUILD NOW:** generic workflow/evidence/policy action classes after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer/product identity isolation, media/document pipeline, approval/audit interfaces.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** warranty rules, product/service integrations, customer portal/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large service-provider network and global claims routing.

# Company 036 — RFP / Tender Intelligence SaaS

**Company ID:** `company:future:036`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:036`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-036-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no live opportunity hunting, bidding, submission or external communication.

## Business identity

Purpose: help organizations analyze RFP/tender packages they already possess or are authorized to process, extract requirements, build compliance matrices and coordinate high-quality response preparation.

Problem: large solicitations contain scattered mandatory requirements, forms, attachments, deadlines and evidence; teams miss items and reuse stale responses.

Value: structured requirements, assignment, evidence-backed drafting, consistency checks and submission-readiness proof.

## Product tree

Solicitation Intake; Document/Attachment Parser; Requirement Extraction; Compliance Matrix; Deadline/Milestone Calendar; Eligibility/Go-No-Go Analysis; Response Outline Builder; Assignment/Collaboration; Response Library; Evidence/Reference Library; Drafting Assistant; Pricing Input Coordinator (not price setter); Form/Attachment Checklist; Consistency/Claim Verification; Page/Word/Format Validation; Security/Legal/Compliance Review Queues; Submission Readiness Gate; Post-Submission Archive; Debrief/Lessons Learned; API/OEM; Industry Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: solicitation/version, issuing entity, deadlines/timezone, mandatory vs scored requirements, pass/fail criteria, evaluation factors, forms, certifications, clauses, references, evidence, owner/assignee, response status, source citation/page, dependencies, questions/clarifications, amendments, approved answer/version, word/page limits, final checklist, audit.

Customers: SMB/enterprise proposal teams, government contractors, B2B vendors, consultants, nonprofits/grant-adjacent procurement respondents, construction/engineering, IT/software/services, manufacturers, staffing, healthcare administrative suppliers.

Verticals: public procurement, enterprise sourcing responses, construction/engineering, technology, professional services, healthcare/admin vendors, education, defense-adjacent only within lawful nonclassified scope. Specialized legal/security packs required for sensitive sectors.

## Brain / architecture

Brain understands solicitation structure, requirements, evaluation criteria and response-library relevance; drafts cited responses and flags unsupported claims. Deterministic checklist/format/deadline/evidence rules own completeness. No live opportunity discovery under this directive; no submission without explicit authorization.

Architecture: document parser/OCR, requirement ontology, dependency graph, response/evidence search/RAG, deadline scheduler, workflow/assignment, LLM drafting with source citations, deterministic validation and version/amendment tracking.

## Agent tree

Solicitation Intake Agent, Requirement Extractor, Compliance Matrix Agent, Eligibility Analyst, Response Planner, Evidence Librarian, Drafting Agent, Consistency/Fact Checker, Amendment Monitor, Pricing Input Coordinator, Security/Compliance Reviewer, Format/Submission QA Agent, Debrief Agent.

## Deterministic services

Document/version store; parser/OCR; requirement registry; deadline/calendar; assignment workflow; response/evidence library; search; form/checklist validator; format/word/page checks; audit; protected submit/send gate.

## Workflow

Import authorized solicitation → verify package/version → parse/extract → classify requirements/deadlines → go/no-go recommendation → assign owners → retrieve approved evidence → draft/review → amendment diff → compliance/format/security QA → submission readiness evidence → owner-authorized submission outside system → archive/debrief/update approved library.

## Integrations / API / data

Document storage, task/project tools, CRM, proposal systems, e-sign, calendars, pricing/ERP inputs, security/compliance evidence, source control for technical responses. APIs for solicitations/requirements/matrix/assignments/evidence/readiness.

Data moat: requirement ontology, reviewed response/evidence mappings, amendment history, win/loss/debrief lessons and vertical packs. No confidential solicitation/customer data cross-sharing.

## Monetization / distribution

Solicitations/users/teams, response-library size, enterprise/private, vertical packs, API/OEM, managed proposal operations. Distribution via proposal/procurement ecosystems, consultants, government-contracting and B2B sales communities; no opportunity hunting now.

## Security/legal/privacy

Confidential bid data, pricing, customer references and security evidence require strict isolation. No fabricated credentials/capabilities, no classified data unless separately designed/authorized, no signature/submission/legal acceptance automation.

## Failure / edge cases

Amendment missed, duplicate conflicting requirement, ambiguous mandatory language, timezone deadline, stale evidence, hallucinated case study, pricing mismatch, form version wrong, attachment omitted, page limit overflow. Use exact source/version/citations, completeness matrix, hard validation and human review.

## Scale / overlap

Small proposal teams → enterprise proposal operations → response intelligence platform. Overlap #31 forms, #23 contracts, #12 compliance, #38 grants. #036 stays solicitation-response intelligence.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** document/version/citation, deadline/dependency, evidence truth, protected submission/communication action.  
**BUILD NOW:** shared document/workspace/approval primitives after reverse-map.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** confidential workspace isolation, submission-gate and response-library interfaces.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer proposal product/templates/packs/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** large enterprise response knowledge network.
